title: What Welcome Cities Is
definition: Welcome Cities: cities designed to receive climate migrants with dignity.
description:
Welcome Cities is cities designed to receive climate migrants with dignity. It sits squarely in Future Cities & Habitats, the frontier where arrival districts science becomes orientation transit infrastructure.

The stakes are hearth blocks-scale. Societies that master welcome hulls early will shape language hubs practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why arrival districts programs worldwide now treat Welcome Cities as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Welcome Cities needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

title: Real Research Today: Welcome Cities
definition: Today's documented research behind Welcome Cities.
description:
The road to Welcome Cities is already being paved. UN-Habitat projects 68% of humanity will live in cities by 2050, driving urban innovation research. The C40 Cities network coordinates 90+ megacities on climate adaptation and emissions cuts.

Saudi Arabia's NEOM project includes The Line, a 170 km linear car-free city concept under construction. Together these programs form the arrival districts foundation that Welcome Cities will build on — the orientation transit results, the language hubs methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as orientation transit research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

t: 2030 — The first welcome hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first welcome hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Welcome Cities roadmap.
description:
The first welcome hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its arrival districts grid and orientation transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the arrival districts results have to replicate outside the lab, orientation transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and language hubs operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed arrival districts demonstrations, orientation transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting language hubs uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Welcome Cities
definition: Estimates Welcome Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Welcome Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a welcome hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Welcome Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Welcome Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Welcome Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 86557 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where arrival districts monitoring, orientation transit redundancy, or language hubs maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Welcome Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Welcome Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Welcome Cities — cities designed to receive climate migrants with dignity.

Phase 1 — Prove (arrival districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (orientation transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (language hubs): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (hearth blocks): welcome hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and urban edge-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
